### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **6** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **90** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**75** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 96b7975b0587bd3268884ea44f3b3170d90187d3`.

⛔ **20** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (symbol, 59 pages)`, `os validate (command, 93 pages)`
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **189** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 96b7975b0587bd3268884ea44f3b3170d90187d3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `78ec27d016cc83838cb53ba1c515abaa0d03c815` — the merge of head `7052770cd8e35f0577a027a6cf69a06dfde0dc19` into base `96b7975b0587bd3268884ea44f3b3170d90187d3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 78ec27d016cc83838cb53ba1c515abaa0d03c815 && git checkout 78ec27d016cc83838cb53ba1c515abaa0d03c815
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 96b7975b0587bd3268884ea44f3b3170d90187d3 7052770cd8e35f0577a027a6cf69a06dfde0dc19 && git checkout -B drift-repro 96b7975b0587bd3268884ea44f3b3170d90187d3 && git merge --no-ff 7052770cd8e35f0577a027a6cf69a06dfde0dc19

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 96b7975b0587bd3268884ea44f3b3170d90187d3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 96b7975b0587bd3268884ea44f3b3170d90187d3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f87f5e242f156a96a4fb7d3052df372aeb29b2cc`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field-customization.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/related-list-entry.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-read-decorations.ts + packages/objectql/src/registry-custom-arrangement.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry-object-registration.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-registration.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry-revision.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-extension-arrangement.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-face.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-list-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-object-extension-item.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/extension-arrangement.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/lint/src/object-graph.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-translation-references.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/deriveRelatedLists.ts, ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/synth/buildDefaultPageSchema.ts (each implementing file read at the hunks of this diff only; code outside the diff was read, not reviewed). Tests, generated baselines, content/docs and the changeset were read as evidence only.

### ① Derived judgments

Check-runs on the head: 70 runs, 61 success, 9 skipped (opt-in and schedule-only jobs), 0 failed, 0 pending. Test Core 10 of 10, Test UI 16 of 16, the Type Check lanes, Lint and Repo Gates, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness and Governed Surface Queue Guard are success. These are the gate verdicts; nothing was re-run.

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies:

- `ObjectExtensionSchema.fieldGroups` (array of `ObjectFieldGroupSchema`) and `ObjectExtensionSchema.relatedLists` (array of `ObjectExtensionRelatedListEntrySchema`): previously refused at parse on every extension by the two `guidance` rows, now accepted at parse on every extension. Widening. Right: a parse does not know the writing package, and the `__c` precedent (ADR-0146 D10) also judges the package at the doors and not in `stack.zod.ts`.
- What that trades away: the refusal of a non-`.custom` writer is no longer at parse. It now sits at item save, restore and draft promotion (`objectExtensionItemRefusal` step 8), `os validate`, `os build` and the marketplace install (step 1c-arrangement); every other entry falls to the registry fold, which skips the key and names it in the boot log. Read in the tree: `mergeObjectDefinitions` copies named keys only, so the two keys reach the object through `applyCustomArrangement` alone, and that function applies a writer only when `isCustomizationPackage(packageId)` holds. So a non-`.custom` extension is never applied at any door; where no door judges it, the outcome is an inert key with a warning, not a refusal. That is the card's item 2 (three doors, on the `__c` precedent) and is right; it is not "refused exactly as before" on three paths, named in N1.
- `ObjectExtensionRelatedListEntryObjectSchema` and its `hidden` key: new. The built-in tab names stay refused in the object form through the inherited `list` pattern (pinned by the spec suite). Right.
- `RelatedListEntryObjectSchema` gains a `hidden` guidance row. `hidden` was already refused there as an unknown key; the refusal stays and gains a sentence. No narrowing.
- New refinements on `ObjectExtensionSchema` (duplicate group keys, the object's two membership rules over the extension's own fields, contradictory shown and hidden entries, `place` beside the key that replaces it): each fires only on an input carrying a key that was refused before. No narrowing.
- `BASE_FIELD_DISPLAY_WHITELIST`: unchanged. Right: `hidden` is read by `packages/objectql/src/search-companion.ts` (a hidden field leaves the companion column) and by the form routes' required reading, so it fails the display-only test the ADR states.
- `METADATA_READ_DECORATIONS` gains `_relatedListsArrangement`. Every strip is list-driven (`stripReadDecorations`, the export strip in `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`, the clone strips), so the new key is stripped on every write and on export with no further edit. It is stamped on the served by-name read and the effective served list only, never on the per-package layer, the execution face or a draft read. Right.
- New exports (`CUSTOM_ARRANGEMENT_KEYS`, `extensionArrangementKeys`, `relatedListEntryHidden`, `relatedListNameCovers`, `RELATED_LISTS_ARRANGEMENT_DECORATION`, `RelatedListsArrangement`, `readRelatedListsArrangement`, the two entry schemas and types; `judgeExtensionArrangement` and its envelope; `SchemaRegistry#getRelatedListsArrangement`): additive. Right.
- `VisibleObjectExtension.fieldGroups` in `@objectstack/lint` is a new required member of an exported interface; additive for readers, and the type lanes are green.

### ② Semver level

The changeset declares `minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, `objectql`, `metadata-protocol`, `cli`, `cloud-connection`, `lint`, `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/plugin-detail`. That matches what the diff publishes: new accepted keys, new exports, one new read decoration, and nothing that refuses an input accepted on `main`. `Check Changeset` is success.

Clause-②: yes (widening) — on the PR body and in the changeset, and it agrees with ①: every changed position accepts more or the same; none narrows. `Metadata-protocol: added` is the lane's declaration and is consistent with a new accepted key and a new served decoration.

One sentence of the changeset overstates (evidence only, the changeset is the lane's): "was already refused at parse, and is still refused" does not hold on the three paths of N1.

### ③ Boundary flags

SQL push-down: no finding. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join; the fold and the readers work on metadata bodies already in memory.

Security: no hunk changes who can read or write a record or a field. A hidden tab and a field in a hidden group are presentation: the list and the field still read over the API under the caller's permissions. The arrangement is written by whoever may write a `.custom` package (the metadata write door's existing authority); the decoration serves a package id and the hidden list names to every reader of the served object, the same class of name an object's own `relatedLists` already serves. One thing to carry into the prose: nothing in the diff teaches hiding as a permission, and nothing says it is not one (part of S3).

The dev's five forks and the sixth `open_questions` row:

1. Several `.custom` writers. The doors judging by the suffix predicate: right as built; the card names the `__c` precedent, and the CLI door has no installed base to ask. The choice among several admitted writers is wrong as built: S2. One part needs the maintainer: a `.custom` package that is not the pair of the object's App, writing alone, is applied (the "else the one folded last" arm). The card says only the paired package (「只对配对的 .custom 包放开」) and ADR-0146 D2 fixes the customer's layer "by role, never by publish order"; neither says whether another App's pair may arrange this object, and the save and install doors could refuse it where the CLI cannot.
2. A list the owner hid by leaving it out stays hidden until the arrangement names it: right as built. It matches the card's purpose for item 4 (what an upgrade or a later package brings is not lost) without revealing what the vendor chose not to show, and it is stated in the key's description. S1 is one case where the build does not keep this rule.
3. `hidden` on relationship entries only: needs the maintainer. The card's item 1 lets the list name the three built-in tabs and item 4 says hiding is written. As built, the environment has no way to hide the attachments tab or the activity stream of an installed object: it cannot leave one out (unlisted shows, or is carried), cannot write `hidden` on it, and cannot patch the object's `enable` keys. The dev's reason for A (a second switch beside the object's own) does not apply to the environment, which holds no first switch. Additive later; nothing built here blocks it, so it is not graded.
4. No field-hide key; a `.custom` group with `visibleWhen: 'false'`: right as built as the mechanism (the card's item 5 delegates the choice to the admission test, and the test is applied correctly). The published wording of the recipe is incomplete: S3.
5. Names not cross-checked against the installed object: right as built. Read in the tree: an unknown field name in a group's `fields` is skipped by `deriveFieldGroupLayout` (the object parse does not judge it either); an unknown list name names no list in `relatedListNamingEntries` and places nothing; an unknown hidden name hides nothing. Not judged at `os validate` or at install. A refusal would make the environment's next save fail after a vendor upgrade removes a field, which the card's "no upgrade-time merging" rules out. A lint warning is a fair follow-up.
6. Skills-docs follow-up (`skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md`): the seat's to file; not judged here.

Other flags:

- Card item 6 (the ADR-0146 D10 note) is not in this PR and is carried by #36086. Until that lands, the note on `main` says the opposite of this code ("the base's arrangement stays the base's", "refused at parse"), and every `[ADR-0146 D10]` tag in the hits files cites a rule the ADR does not yet state. The PR body says `Fixes #36498`, which closes the card with item 6 and the skills follow-up still owed; the seat should keep the card or a named follow-up open.
- Overlap: draft #36399 edits another region of `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`; the later lander merges `main`. Note only.
- The path from the served read to the two readers is pinned on each side (the protocol suite serves the decoration; the two reader suites take it as input) and by no end-to-end case. The console already passes underscore keys of a served object through to `deriveRelatedLists` (`_packageId`), so no strip is expected; not graded.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/data/field-customization.ts` — holds. `CUSTOM_ARRANGEMENT_KEYS` is the one list the fold and the judge both read through `extensionArrangementKeys`; "written" includes an empty array, which the fold and the spec suite agree on. The `hidden` paragraph agrees with the code it cites.

`packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-read-decorations.ts` — holds; see ①.

`packages/spec/src/data/related-list-entry.ts` — `relatedListNameCovers`, `relatedListEntryHidden` and `readRelatedListsArrangement` hold against their consumers, with one gap in what `RelatedListsArrangement` can say (S1).

`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` — the two keys, the entry schema and the five refinements hold against the card's items 1 to 4 and against the fold. Findings S1 and S3 touch its published descriptions.

S1 (should-fix) — hiding every tab of a declared tab list reveals the lists the owner hid. Trace: the owner declares `relatedLists: ['a', 'b']` and leaves its own child list `c` out; the `.custom` extension writes `relatedLists: [{ list: 'a', hidden: true }, { list: 'b', hidden: true }]`. In `applyCustomArrangement`, `shown` is empty and `carried` is empty (both entries are covered), so the served `relatedLists` is `[]` with the decoration `unlisted: 'hidden'`. In `deriveRelatedLists`, `relatedListNamingEntries` answers `null` for an empty list ("absent, or empty"), and the loop's `if (!naming)` arm pushes every list not hidden by name, so `c` now shows, and so does every other own-package list the owner left out. The same happens with a one-entry owner list whose entry is hidden. This contradicts the key's own description ("A list the object's own `relatedLists` hides by leaving it out stays hidden until this list names it"), the decoration's `unlisted: 'hidden'` ("the served list's own rule") and fork 2 as built. No suite covers the case (the fold suite hides one of several; the reader suite's `hidden` control uses a non-empty list). A served empty list cannot say "declared, and nothing shows", so the fix belongs in the reader's reading of the decoration or in what the fold serves; either moves the head. Presentation only: no record becomes readable that was not.

S2 (should-fix) — the choice among several `.custom` writers does not know the App pair. `registry-custom-arrangement.ts` picks the first admitted writer for which `isCustomizationPairOf(writer.packageId, context.ownerPackageId)` holds, else the writer folded last. ADR-0146 D3 as amended makes the unit the App: the pair of an object owned by a module of an App is the App's `.custom` package, and `packages/metadata-core/src/customization-pair-lookup.ts` states the rule for every caller: ask `pairOf` or `isPairOf`, never `isCustomizationPairOf(pair, base)` directly. For an object a module owns (the HotCRM shape the card is accepted against), the predicate never matches the real pair, so with two `.custom` writers the one served is decided by fold order, which ADR-0146 D2 rules out for the customer's layer ("by role, never by publish order"), and the boot log may name the real pair as the one skipped. The module's jsdoc and the changeset both say "the pair of the object's owner is served". With one writer the fallback serves it, which is why every suite is green; the two-writer case in the fold suite uses an owner that is its own unit. The registry already resolves pairs through `pairOf` with the installed manifests (`registry.ts`, the holder lookup), so the fold's context can carry the pair id.

S3 (should-fix) — the published recipe for hiding a base field omits what it breaks. The `fieldGroups` description in `object.zod.ts`, the `BASE_FIELD_DISPLAY_WHITELIST` jsdoc, the docs page and the changeset prescribe a group whose `visibleWhen` is false, and the PR body says it "changes nothing else". Read in the tree: a field claimed by a hidden section is not mounted, and the form skips the unmounted control at submit-time validation (`ui/packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx`, `hiddenSectionFieldNames`), while the server still requires it. So a base field that is `required` with no default, hidden this way, makes the create form unsubmittable: the save is refused naming a field the user cannot see. The repo already treats this hazard as blocking on form views (`requiredInGatedSection.ts`). The recipe also does not say that the field stays readable and writable over the API, the sentence `ObjectFieldGroupSchema.requiresFeature` carries for the same mechanism ("Presentation only"). The description should say both: not for a required field without a default, and not access control. Read from the code, not run.

Implementing files, against the contract:

- `registry-custom-arrangement.ts` — agrees with the description sentence by sentence apart from S1 and S2. Checked by reading: a key not written keeps steps 1 and 2; a listed field's `group` follows the listing group and a non-listed field of the owner or another extension loses a `group` naming a listing or missing group, so the served object still passes the object's two membership rules; a bare child covers its relationships in both the carry-over and the hiding; carried entries go before a trailing approvals and stream run; nothing is stored, and the decoration is keyed on the served body.
- `registry-object-registration.ts`, `registry.ts`, `engine-registration.ts`, `registry-revision.ts` — agree: the step runs after `applyExtensionPlacements`, the contribution carries the two keys, the accessor reads the served fold's own body.
- `protocol-extension-arrangement.ts`, `protocol-object-extension-item.ts` — agree: one judge, refusal in every non-`.custom` package, prescription inside the message, the item door asks it after the binding check (an item bound to no package is refused earlier at step 1).
- `protocol-meta-item-face.ts`, `protocol-meta-list-reads.ts` — agree: the decoration rides the faces `_withheldFields` rides and no other.
- `cli/src/utils/extension-arrangement.ts`, `compile.ts`, `validate.ts` — agree, and validate and build call the same function (parity roster row present).
- `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` — agrees: every delivered package is judged before any write, 422 with one row per key.
- `lint/src/object-graph.ts`, `validate-translation-references.ts` — agree with the widened surface; the dev's note that a `place`-brought group is probably still not a section anchor predates this PR and is not this diff's.
- `deriveRelatedLists.ts`, `buildDefaultPageSchema.ts` — agree with `RelatedListsArrangement` as documented, and are inert with no decoration; S1 is the case the documented shape cannot express.

N1 (nit) — three paths accept a non-`.custom` writer's key where `main` refused it at parse, each ending in the fold's skip and boot-log line: a code-defined stack that boots without `os validate` or `os build`; a stack naming no package id, which `os validate` now passes (`judgeExtensionArrangement` skips a subject with no package id, though no `.custom` package can be the writer there); and the package duplicate and orphan adoption in `protocol-package-commits.ts`, where the `__c` judge is asked and this one is not (not verified whether the copy loop routes an `object_extension` row through the save door). Nothing is misapplied on any of them. Follow-up card, not a change on this head.

N2 (nit) — `content/docs/data-modeling/object-extensions.mdx` and the changeset repeat the recipe of S3 and the "pair of the object's owner" wording of S2; they follow whatever those fixes say.

S1, S2 and S3 are open on this head and earn a delta review of their fixes. Forks 1 (the lone non-pair writer) and 3 go to the maintainer.
